risk.line: HIGH, held for a fifth consecutive pass, and the reason to hold it on the day the world acquired a SECOND contested chokepoint is that the gate this board publishes is written in hulls and bodies, not in maps. A struck US-flagged merchant hull or a confirmed American death: not today, again. What did happen is a change in the KIND of risk rather than its level, and it is the change this desk has been watching for since June. Ansar Allah took Mocha, pushed on to Dhubab and claims Zuqar island, which means the Yemeni bank of Bab el-Mandeb - twenty-nine kilometres of water carrying roughly a tenth of world seaborne trade - is now held on the ground rather than merely threatened from the air. The measurement arrived within hours: twelve vessels crossed on Thursday against thirty on Wednesday, with ONE entering the Red Sea against seventeen. That is the difference between a missile campaign, which can be intercepted and deterred, and a shore battery, which has to be taken back by infantry. Saudi Arabia answered with fifty-four air strikes and took ballistic missiles and drones at Khamis Mushait, Abha and Jazan for its trouble, and Pakistan told Tehran that the Mecca defence pact 'will definitely make this agreement operational' if the aggression spills further into the kingdom - a nuclear-armed state publicly attaching itself to the Saudi side of an Iranian proxy war. The price board answered through the middle of the economy: Brent closed $101.21 on Wednesday and trades $105 to $107, the US diesel crack is at an all-time $108 a barrel with pump diesel at a record $5.967, the ten-year is 4.95 and the thirty-year 5.36, and the Money Printer board flipped YELLOW to RED with three of four live lines crossed. The ECB hiked into it this morning; the Fed decides in six days. Two chokepoints, two central banks tightening into an energy shock, and a ledger question that broke its barrier and gave this board the first score it has ever taken. The gate is still, precisely, unmet - and saying so on a day like this is the whole point of having written it down in advance.

forecasts.q: US diesel crack spread settles back below $45/bbl before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: CUT 3 on a genuinely new variable, and the variable is the ROUTE rather than the barrel or the refinery. This question has been marked down twice already - once on crude-conversion scarcity, once on physical damage to Jazan's conversion capacity. Today's fact is neither: Ansar Allah took Mocha and the Yemeni coast at Bab el-Mandeb, and transits through the strait fell from thirty on Wednesday to twelve on Thursday with a single vessel entering the Red Sea against seventeen the day before. Bab el-Mandeb is the door through which Gulf and Indian diesel reaches Europe; close it and the arbitrage that normally pulls a record crack back toward $45 has to sail around the Cape, adding roughly two weeks and burning the same fuel it is carrying. Hirschman's point about substitutability is the mechanism: a spread mean-reverts when a cheaper source can physically reach the expensive market, and the cheap source just got two weeks further away. Diesel is at a record $5.967 a gallon with the crack at an all-time $108. Capped at 3 because a Cape reroute is expensive, not impossible, and because Atlantic-basin refiners can still supply Europe at a price.

forecasts.q: The FOMC raises the fed funds target range at or before the 9-10 December 2026 meeting
forecasts.note: RAISE 2, deliberately small, and the framework that argues AGAINST it is named and priced rather than mentioned. The ECB raised to 2.5 per cent this morning and said explicitly that it is preparing for LONGER-LASTING inflation - a peer central bank publicly abandoning look-through on the same energy shock, which raises the reputational cost to the FOMC of doing the opposite. US producer prices came in firmer in the details, Brent is $105 to $107, and the horizon here contains THREE meetings, not one, so this is not a bet on Wednesday alone. Against it stands Blinder and Bernanke's finding that central banks have generally and correctly looked THROUGH supply shocks, and the fact that core PPI printed 0.2 against 0.3 expected - the single number still saying this is energy rather than a general inflation. The offset is why this is +2 and not +8. Anchor held at 50: the reference class is a hawkish-chair committee with three standing dissents and three meetings left, and nothing today changes that class.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: CUT 2, and it is the first VOLUME print this question has been given in a fortnight rather than another announcement. Hormuz transits fell to seven on Wednesday against a ten-day average of fourteen; this question needs roughly SIXTY-FIVE a day. The direction of the only admissible evidence class is down, and the level is now four to five per cent of the pre-war baseline rather than the fifty per cent the question asks for. The base rate is the discipline and it is unforgiving: the Suez Canal, closed by a land power holding one bank in June 1967, reopened in June 1975 - eight years - and the Nimbus Moon clearance operation alone took roughly a year AFTER the political agreement to reopen. There is no agreement text here at all. Anchor recomputed 12 to 10, dated today, inputs: seven transits observed 09-09, ten-day average fourteen, baseline about 130. Held to two points because floor effects are real - at four per cent of baseline the remaining downside is small and the question is now almost entirely a bet on whether a political settlement arrives, not on the tape.

forecasts.q: The Algeria-UAE rupture turns material: Algeria names a UAE commercial interest for cancellation or seizure
forecasts.note: OPENED at 40, and it pays a coverage debt this book has named on four separate days without paying: AFRICA has been carried by GEO-023, which is a RUSSIA question that happens to be set in Africa. Resolution: Algeria publicly cancels, suspends, expropriates or refuses to renew a NAMED Emirati commercial interest - port, telecom, energy, logistics or a sovereign-fund stake - before 2027-03-31, per Reuters, AP or AFP. The object exists and is unusually concrete: DP World holds thirty-year concessions over the container terminals at Algiers and Djen-Djen through fifty-fifty joint ventures with the Algerian port authorities, employing more than eight hundred people, with about $108m of committed upgrade capex. BASE RATE first: of the clearest modern ruptures between Arab or Muslim states, three of four produced a material economic instrument within months - Qatar 2017 (blockade), Algeria-Morocco 2021 (the Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline not renewed), Saudi-Canada 2018 (trade and student freeze) - against Turkey-UAE 2018-19, which stayed rhetorical. That is the 40. It is not higher because Algeria's leverage over Abu Dhabi is thin and the terminals are jointly owned, so seizing them damages Algerian throughput first; it is not lower because Algiers has done exactly this before, to Rabat, on a bigger asset.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: CUT 2 after two sessions of deliberate holds, and the dated falsifier published on 09-06 has now RUN. It said the capitals pause would be informative if it lapsed with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text. It lapsed exactly on schedule and Russia put 166 drones, 32 cruise missiles and ballistic and anti-ship rounds into Ukraine within hours, killing five and wounding 63. A truce whose duration matches an envoy's itinerary to the hour is a scheduling accommodation, not a de-escalation - and it demonstrates that Moscow can switch the air campaign on and off at will, which is evidence of confidence rather than exhaustion. Fortna's condition is used a third time and now in the direction that costs us: no monitors, no guarantor, no demarcation, and now a scored falsifier. Only 2 points because Zelenskyy simultaneously said talks are possible this month, and a party that expects to meet is not a party that has walked.

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: CUT 2, and the discipline is separating the new fact from the loud one. The loud fact is a record surplus: exports up 25 per cent, the August surplus $119.1bn against $112.5bn in July, $805.5bn year to date, shipments to the US up 34.4 per cent. That is a KNOWN structural condition - China ran $1.2tn last year - and known conditions do not move probabilities. The new fact is that both governments are exploring reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each side, which is the first numbered de-escalation the file has produced since the May truce, sixteen days before a state visit. Composition reinforces it: the surge is in semiconductors, computing hardware and AI-adjacent goods, meaning American demand is pulling the flow. A country importing what it needs is a country that renews.

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly moves toward enrichment or the bomb
forecasts.note: RAISED 2, the smaller of today's two raises, on a demonstrated air-defence shortfall rather than on any nuclear signal. Drones and ballistic missiles reached a coalition airbase at Khamis Mushait and Aramco sites at Abha, Najran and Jazan, wounding 73, on top of direct Iranian strikes on Ras Tanura and Prince Sultan Air Base between February and June. Sagan's security model is the framework: proliferation pressure rises when a state's protector visibly cannot cover it, and Riyadh's revealed strategy through this entire war has been to convert insecurity into a HIGHER PRICE for the American guarantee rather than into an independent programme. That is why this is +2 and not +6 - what today buys is leverage in a guarantee negotiation, and only the failure of that negotiation would buy a programme.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: RAISED 1 to the anchor, and a one-point move is all an expected event confirming on schedule is worth. Sixteen days out, with reporting now describing a concrete pre-summit deliverable under negotiation - reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each way - rather than only logistics. A summit with a numbered agenda item is marginally harder to cancel than a summit with a guest list.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: HELD, and this is today's most important non-move. Iranian-aligned forces struck four Saudi cities and halted operations at energy facilities; the intuitive read is that an attack on a US ally's oil raises the odds of American strikes on Iran. The base rate says the opposite, and it is the single most relevant analog available: Abqaiq, 14 September 2019, took 5.7 million barrels a day off line - half of Saudi output, the most damaging attack ever on oil infrastructure - was attributed by Washington to Iran directly, and produced NO American strike on Iran. What it produced was a troop deployment and a sanctions round. Damage to Saudi assets has never been the trigger; damage to American ones has. The 09-06 resolution-criteria pin is restated verbatim and still binds: multi-day, state targets inside Iran.

forecasts.q: IF a Hormuz deal happens, it preserves Iranian transit administration
forecasts.note: HELD. Qatar asking for UNCONDITIONAL reopening is, read carefully, evidence on the other side of this question - an unconditional reopening is precisely one that preserves no administrative machinery. But Qatar's ask is not a deal term, and this question resolves on what an agreement CONTAINS, not on what a third party requests. Ostovar's mechanism is unchanged: the Guard converts each crisis into an institution that outlives it.

forecasts.q: Yen carry stress: USD/JPY appreciates 8%+ (160 to 147.2 or below) in any 30-day window
forecasts.note: HELD, and the reason is logged as a limitation rather than a judgement: no fresh USD/JPY print was established in today's reading, and yesterday's 154.06 was already priced. FRED still carries a lagged 159.97 from 28 August, so the board's own series cannot see the move. Moving a barrier question without a current spot would be exactly the error the 09-06 anchor rule was written to stop.

forecasts.q: An AfD politician is sworn in as Minister-President of a German Land
forecasts.note: HELD the day after a seven-point raise, which is the correct shape - the ballot arithmetic that bought those points has not changed and yesterday's move already priced it. Today added protests across Germany and a Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote on 20 September. Street mobilisation against the AfD is precisely the variable that failed in Saxony-Anhalt, where turnout rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent and the AfD still gained; so it is logged as evidence with no directional signal until the 20 September result.

forecasts.q: Israel-Hezbollah escalates to multi-week campaign
forecasts.note: HELD. No new Lebanon tempo established in today's reading after yesterday's +3 on the deadliest two-day stretch since the June truce. Nothing today, and a raise on yesterday's casualties would be a double-count.

forecasts.q: Fed's standing T-bill purchase program still running at end-2026
forecasts.note: HELD for the ninth session. Balance sheet $6.74tn and rising, ON RRP at $0.68bn with no buffer left, no sunset language. Today's UK long-end print is the argument FOR this question rather than against it: the bill programme repairs the short end, which is exactly why the thirty-year leg keeps repricing without it.

forecasts.q: Hormuz at full pre-war normal
forecasts.note: HELD for the eleventh day. Same framework as GEO-001 at a harder bar. Qatar's appeal was spent there and cannot be spent twice.

forecasts.q: US Hormuz concession within 30 days after the Xi summit
forecasts.note: HELD. Two-sided again. Qatar carrying the Hormuz file to Beijing sixteen days before the summit raises the chance the strait is ON the agenda, which is a precondition for a concession; but a widened regional war with an ally's refineries burning is the environment in which concessions get postponed, not signed.

forecasts.q: US commits to fixed Venezuelan heavy-crude export infrastructure
forecasts.note: HELD. No dredging contract, no terminal tender, no published instrument. The premeditation tell requires a document, and none appeared. Brent at $99 raises the commercial logic for a heavy-barrel hedge without being evidence that anyone has signed for one.

forecasts.q: US sanctions a top-10 Chinese bank before the Xi summit
forecasts.note: HELD. Sixteen days, no blocking designation, and a live $30bn reciprocal tariff-cut negotiation makes a bank designation less likely rather than more. Farrell and Newman: the hammer that hangs is worth more than the hammer that falls.

forecasts.q: Economic D-Day works: China cuts Iranian oil >50%, sustained
forecasts.note: HELD. Nothing today touched Beijing's Iranian purchases. Qatar lobbying Wang Yi on the strait is an approach to China as a mediator, which is a different transaction from China cutting its own barrels. Drezner: intensity is not compliance.

forecasts.q: Russian Q4 territorial gains fall below the Q2-Q3 average
forecasts.note: HELD. A 166-drone night is an air-campaign event, not a line-of-contact one, and this question resolves on ground taken. Autumn mud then winter depress mechanised advance in the historical series; the counter-argument is that a Russia demonstrating it controls the tempo may be husbanding for a winter push.

forecasts.q: IF Ukraine fighting stops 30+ days pre-2028: armistice, no peace treaty
forecasts.note: HELD, and today strengthened it without justifying a move, because it is already high. A pause that exists only as an unwritten understanding covering a visit, which lapses on a clock with no text on either side, is the exact ancestor of the Korean 1953 shape this question describes.

forecasts.q: Mojtaba makes a verified live public appearance
forecasts.note: HELD. No authenticated video or audio. Iran's public voice on the Saudi strikes was the Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree, not Tehran - which is the point of a proxy and also, incidentally, another day without the Supreme Leader on camera.

forecasts.q: Security-elite fracture in Iran (IRGC defection, coup, mass purge)
forecasts.note: HELD. No defection, coup indicator or purge reported. A widened proxy front is evidence of command coherence, not fracture.

forecasts.q: China stands up a third physical-gold venue or a delivery-forcing mechanism
forecasts.note: HELD. GVZ at 27.18 is a stress proxy, not a venue. This resolves on a named mechanism that forces physical delivery against Western paper pricing, and none was announced.

forecasts.q: China quarantine or blockade of Taiwan
forecasts.note: HELD. No mobilisation indicator. A state running record export volumes into the market it would have to blockade past is not assembling the balance sheet of a quarantine.

forecasts.q: Bitcoin's cycle top prints at or below ~$150k
forecasts.note: HELD. The adoption-saturation model resolves on a price top. Today's relevant cross-current is the long end - a 5.89 per cent thirty-year gilt raises the discount rate on every long-duration asset, which is a headwind the model does not contain.

forecasts.q: Russia's Sahel guarantee formalizes: acknowledged combat deployment in a new African state, or a published defence/basing treaty
forecasts.note: HELD on its ninth day. Today's Africa wires were Sudan - MSF warning the health system is near collapse and a push to widen the arms embargo - plus Boko Haram and ISWAP repelled at a Borno base. No Russian deployment or treaty. The AFRICA coverage debt named yesterday is restated, not discharged.

forecasts.q: India restores the Indus Waters Treaty or resumes Permanent Indus Commission participation
forecasts.note: HELD on its eighth day. No commission meeting. Today's South Asia wire was the Maldives inviting Britain to talks over Chagos, which is a different sovereignty file entirely.

forecasts.q: US publicly departs from formal neutrality on Falklands sovereignty
forecasts.note: HELD on its fifth day, and today produced the file's first genuinely related noise - Itamar Ben-Gvir urging sanctions on Britain over its 'occupation of the Falklands' in retaliation for the settlement trade ban. That is an Israeli minister's rhetorical counterpunch, not a State Department document, and this question resolves on a US instrument. Logged so the temptation is on the record and refused.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Houthis take Mokha and traffic through Bab el-Mandeb collapses
brief.h: Ansar Allah seized the last government-held Red Sea port south of Hodeidah and pushed on to Dhubab, and transits through the strait fell from thirty on Wednesday to twelve on Thursday, with a single vessel entering the Red Sea against seventeen the day before.
brief.t: The important thing here is not that a Yemeni town changed hands - it is that a threat became a piece of ground. For two years the Red Sea has been closed and reopened by missiles, which can be shot down, deterred, and paid for one at a time. Holding the coast at Bab el-Mandeb, twenty-nine kilometres across at its narrowest, converts that into artillery and shore-launched systems fired from cover, and there is no interceptor for geography: the only way to reverse it is infantry that the Saudi-backed coalition has just demonstrated it does not have. The Giants Brigades, Nation's Shield, the National Resistance and the Taizi units withdrew south after days of fighting, and Riyadh answered with fifty-four air strikes - which is what a coalition does when it has aircraft and no ground force. Follow the money and the second chokepoint pays two people: Tehran, which now rents a second hand on world trade without spending an Iranian life, and Ansar Allah, which gets a revenue and prestige asset it has wanted since 2015. The bill lands somewhere almost nobody is naming, on which more below.
brief.context: R0, date the rail. This is not the Sound Dues and it is not Hormuz; the correct deep-time analogue is the SUEZ CLOSURE of June 1967, the last time a land power holding one bank shut a canal-dependent route - and it stayed shut until June 1975, with the Nimbus Moon clearance operation alone consuming roughly a year AFTER the political decision to reopen. Eight years is the base rate for bank-held waterways, against weeks for missile campaigns, and that asymmetry is the entire forecast. The DESK that decides whether the strait is 'closed' is not CENTCOM and not Riyadh: it is the Lloyd's Joint War Committee and the owners' protection-and-indemnity clubs in London, because a strait shuts when a war-risk quotation stops distinguishing one class of tonnage from another. Lloyd's List Intelligence published the industry's working assumption before Mocha fell - that the Houthi threat was addressed to Saudi-linked hulls rather than the general trade - and Thursday's thirty-to-twelve print is the first evidence that the distinction is dissolving. The influence map: PRINCIPAL Tehran, AGENT Ansar Allah with war aims of its own, NARRATOR the 'Yemeni sovereignty' framing on one side and Saudi briefings about an 'Assad scenario' on the other, OPERATOR the underwriter and the shore battery, MARKET Brent at $107 and war-risk at half a per cent of hull value, TARGET Egypt - whose Suez receipts are a top-three foreign-currency earner and which is on an IMF programme, and which lost roughly sixty per cent of those receipts the last time this route was disrupted. The incompetence alternative, which this desk thinks carries at least half the weight: the defending coalition is a patchwork of rival Saudi- and Emirati-funded militias that has never had a unified command, and Mocha may simply have fallen because its paymasters are feuding - Algiers breaking with Abu Dhabi on the same day is a small tell of how fractious Gulf client management has become. A planned-design read is admissible ONLY because a rail predates the headline: the Houthis publicly declared a Bab el-Mandeb blockade in July and Yemen's government warned of a seizure plan before the advance. Falsifier, dated: weekly transits recovering to roughly 270 by 30 September, or a war-risk quote that still distinguishes Saudi-linked tonnage, means Mocha bought position rather than closure.

angles.effect: Gains a second hand on world trade at no cost in Iranian lives, and a bargaining chip that is separable from the Hormuz file - it can be traded away without Iran conceding anything itself

Loses the coastal buffer that kept the war away from its own energy assets, and takes ballistic missiles at Khamis Mushait, Abha and Jazan in return for fifty-four air strikes that cannot retake ground
Pays the bill nobody is naming: Suez transit fees are a top-three hard-currency earner for a country under an IMF programme, and this is the second Red Sea disruption in three years
Absorb the cost directly - Gulf and Indian distillate reaching Europe now faces a Cape reroute of roughly two extra weeks, into a market already at a record crack spread

dec.kill: The Houthi claim is of UNCONTESTED control of the whole chokepoint coastline including Zuqar island. Mocha is confirmed by geolocated footage; the islands are not. A geolocated image or verified satellite pass placing Houthi forces on Zuqar or the Hanish group confirms the claim; seventy-two hours of repeated Mocha confirmation with no island geolocation means the claim has outrun the evidence.

consp.claim: Imageboard threads are running the seizure as a scripted humiliation rather than a battlefield event - the loudest version reads 'Saudis getting raped this hard mere days after their shills announced Assad scenario for Houthis', arguing the Saudi-briefed 'Assad scenario' story was a tell that Riyadh knew a collapse was coming and was pre-seeding a narrative. A parallel thread insists Ansar Allah 'seized the entire coastline, including Mocha, last night and are still advancing' with 'uncontested control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait', running ahead of any wire confirmation, and a separate line claims the US somehow handed Iran a year-old underwater drone.
consp.spread: Two /pol/ threads doing 178 and 106 replies within hours of the first geolocation, cross-posted from X war-account screenshots; a matching /biz/ line that oil is being walked to $150 on purpose.
consp.read: This maps onto the 'they knew' frame, and the checkable kernel is narrow but real: the Yemeni government publicly warned of a Houthi plan to seize Bab el-Mandeb before it happened, so foreknowledge of INTENT is documented and unremarkable - it is not evidence of collusion. The coastline claim is downstream of a single genuine geolocation of Mocha's main street that then got generalised to islands nobody has imaged, which is the standard way an OSINT confirmation becomes an overclaim. The 'Assad scenario' item is the more interesting one: a briefing campaign that promises a client's collapse days before the client collapses is usually incompetence caught on the record, not a script.

brief.head: Brent breaks $100 and two central banks tighten into the shock
brief.h: Brent closed $101.21 on Wednesday and trades $105 to $107, breaking a band this board had been scoring since 25 August; the ECB raised rates to 2.5 per cent this morning citing longer-lasting inflation, and the Fed decides in six days with the Money Printer board flipped to RED.
brief.t: Start with the number that could embarrass us, because it did the opposite: this desk published a forecast on 25 August that Brent would stay inside $80 to $100 through 24 September, marked it at 65 per cent, and cut it to 17 by 8 September on a barrier recalculation that had nothing to do with opinion. Brent closed $101.21 the next day. That is the first question this ledger has ever resolved, and it scores well - which is worth exactly as much as the method that produced it and nothing more. The machine underneath is the more important story. A central bank sets the price of money; it cannot manufacture diesel. Yet the ECB hiked this morning on 'longer-lasting' inflation and futures put the Fed at roughly two-thirds to hike on Wednesday, six days after Brent broke and with the US diesel crack at an all-time $108 a barrel. Tightening does not add a barrel. What it does is raise the cost of carrying the roughly $40tn of federal debt whose interest bill is already the fastest-growing line in the budget - which is why the thirty-year sits at 5.36 per cent.
brief.context: R0: this is the E6 rail - the 2008-2022 quantitative-easing regime in its unwind chapter - meeting the E4 rail, the 1973 security-for-barrels bargain, at the auction desk. The old rail was a central bank acting as the price-insensitive marginal buyer of long duration; the new permit is that it is now a seller, and the private buyers replacing it are being asked to price thirty years of inflation during a war over the world's principal oil chokepoint. The mechanism to hold is the SPLIT CURVE, and it is Du and Duffie's point: the stablecoin bid and the Fed's standing bill programme repair the FRONT of the curve - the three-month bill sits placidly at 3.80 per cent - and do nothing whatever for duration, which is why the ten-year is 4.95 and the thirty-year 5.36 while the short end naps. The framework arguing the other way, and it is a strong one, is Blinder and Bernanke's finding that central banks have generally been RIGHT to look through supply shocks, because a barrel price is a relative price and not a monetary phenomenon; core PPI printing 0.2 against 0.3 expected is the single number still supporting that read. So the honest statement is that the FOMC is choosing between two respectable frameworks under a new chair whose cheapest available purchase is credibility. The base rate for the ledger question is not a single meeting: three meetings remain before 31 December, which is why it sits at 65 rather than at the odds on Wednesday alone. Falsifier, dated: if core CPI next week comes in soft and the Fed holds anyway, the look-through read wins and GEO-029 should be cut hard; if they hike into a soft core, this is about the chair's credibility rather than about barrels, and that is a different and more durable regime.

consp.claim: The markets board is running two linked lines. First, that the promised $5,000-per-adult payment is not a vote-buying exercise but a tell - 'wildly successful, popular administration, economic golden age... What's the angle here, genuinely? We don't need to buy votes. Why promise 1+ trillion dollars for an assured victory?' - the implication being that someone inside knows a break is coming. Second, that the oil move is engineered rather than physical, with threads insisting '$150 IS ABOUT TO BE REALITY' and 'the delulu market is just slowly coming to terms', alongside an 'EXIT ALL MARKETS NOW' thread and a bond-market thread whose framing slides into an ethnic-scapegoat register.
consp.spread: /biz/ and /pol/ simultaneously - a diesel-record thread, a $5,000-stimulus thread asking specifically about the effect on the 10-year and 30-year, and a 'bond market is imploding' thread; the last one is where the scapegoat framing appears.
consp.read: An ethnic-scapegoat narrative is circulating around the bond selloff; the technique is substitution of an agent for a mechanism - naming a group is cognitively cheaper than pricing duration risk, and it is reported here as a phenomenon rather than repeated. The checkable kernel in the first claim is genuinely good and this desk shares the question: a large untargeted transfer announced eight weeks before an election, into a supply-constrained economy, is inflationary at exactly the moment the central bank is tightening, and the boards spotted the fiscal-monetary collision before most commentary did. The boring explanation is the sufficient one - promises of this shape have been made twice already this cycle, the DOGE dividend and the tariff cheque, and neither was ever paid.

brief.head: Algeria cuts ties with the UAE and gives its envoy 48 hours
brief.h: Algiers summoned the Emirati ambassador, told him relations were severed over 'provocative and hostile actions', gave him two days to comply, and pointedly declined to name the single event that caused it.
brief.t: The missing event is the analysis. When a foreign ministry says it has 'exhausted all means' and then refuses to cite a trigger, it is telling you the cause is cumulative and structural rather than an incident - and the structure here is a proxy contest in the Sahel that neither capital wants to name out loud. Algeria's whole security doctrine is a buffer of friendly or at least neutral southern neighbours; a run of coups in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger dissolved it, and the states that emerged went shopping for patrons. Abu Dhabi has been the most energetic buyer - ports, logistics, security packages, drone sales - across precisely the arc Algiers regards as its own approaches. Layer the older files on top: the UAE normalised with Israel while Algeria remains the loudest Arab holdout, and the two sit on opposite sides of Western Sahara, where Abu Dhabi backs Rabat. Follow the money and the interesting fact is that the rupture is asymmetric - Algeria has far more Emirati capital inside its borders than the reverse, which means the escalation options run one way.
brief.context: The DESK that decides this is not the foreign ministry; it is the Algerian presidency sitting on top of the ANP, the army that has been the real constituency of every Algerian government since 1962, and whose institutional interest is a rentier settlement funded by gas exports and a quiet southern border. On the Emirati side the operative instrument is not diplomacy either - it is the sovereign-fund and ports network, which is how Abu Dhabi converts money into position. That makes the observable concrete: DP World holds thirty-year concessions over the container terminals at Algiers and Djen-Djen through fifty-fifty joint ventures with the Algerian port authorities, employing more than eight hundred people. That is the seizable object, and whether Algiers names it is the test of whether this is a gesture or an instrument. BASE RATE: ruptures of this shape usually do produce a material economic instrument - Qatar 2017 produced a blockade, Algeria-Morocco 2021 produced the non-renewal of the Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline, Saudi-Canada 2018 produced a trade and student freeze; Turkey-UAE 2018-19 stayed rhetorical. Three of four. They also LAST: Algiers and Rabat have been severed for five years with no sign of repair, because a rupture between states with no shared border and modest trade is cheap to maintain and expensive to reverse politically. So the forecast class is durability rather than escalation, and the theatre to watch is not the Maghreb but Libya, where both states already fund opposing structures. A new ledger question, GEO-030, is opened on the material-instrument test at 40 per cent, resolving 31 March 2027.

brief.head: Russia says it foiled a Ukrainian plot against Britain's envoy
brief.h: The FSB says it detained a Russian security officer at the British embassy in Moscow whom it claims the SBU recruited to prepare an attack on Ambassador Nigel Casey that would be blamed on Russia and drag London into the war; neither Kyiv nor the embassy has confirmed anything.
brief.t: Do not read this as a warning about an attack. Read it as a case file. The stated story is a Ukrainian false-flag; the incentive read is that the FSB has just manufactured legal grounds to expel British diplomats, criminalise the embassy's local staff, and acquire a prisoner with a confession - all without firing anything. That is the boring, high-base-rate explanation, and it is the one this desk carries. There is a second reading, and honesty requires naming it: Russia has a documented habit of publicly accusing an adversary of the thing it is about to do, most famously the 2022 'dirty bomb' campaign and the Donbas genocide claims that preceded the invasion. But note what actually happened after those: the alleged Ukrainian act never occurred in any of them. A pattern of accusations that are never followed by the accused event is not a warning signal - it is a rhetorical instrument with a very poor predictive record, and treating it as a countdown is how a reader gets played twice.
brief.context: The mechanism is what Paul and Matthews called the firehose of falsehood: high-volume, multichannel, rapid and unconcerned with consistency, because the goal is not to be believed but to make the audience treat all accounts as equally unreliable. The DESK here is the FSB's counterintelligence directorate, not the foreign ministry - and its institutional incentive is cases closed and detainees held, which is exactly the product this announcement generates. Set it beside the week's other Ukraine facts and the shape is clearer: Zelenskyy is in Canada asking Mark Carney for air defence ahead of a winter in which Russia is again targeting the grid; the WSJ reports European capitals struggling with the rising cost of underwriting Ukraine's defence. Russia's cheapest available weapon against a coalition that is running out of money is not a missile, it is a story that makes the most expensive members wonder whether they are being manoeuvred. INFLUENCE MAP: PRINCIPAL the Kremlin, AGENT the FSB, NARRATOR state media plus the named blogger the FSB conveniently attributes the tasking to, OPERATOR the accreditation office that can expel diplomats, TARGET the British parliamentary majority that has to keep voting the money. Falsifier with a window: if within 30 days Moscow expels UK diplomats, restricts consular services, or brings the detainee to a televised confession, the legal-groundwork read is confirmed. If instead an actual incident occurs at a Western mission in Moscow, the pre-accusation read scores and this desk was wrong.

angles.effect: Books a counterintelligence success, a detainee and a legal basis for expulsions - the whole product is generated by the announcement itself
Injects doubt into the British domestic argument about funding Ukraine at the exact moment European capitals are struggling with the cost
Pay in embassy operating capacity and in the time spent denying an unfalsifiable claim - the denial is itself the amplification
Bears the entire physical cost of the operation, a Russian national with no seat at any of these tables

dec.kill: An expulsion order or a televised confession within 30 days confirms the legal-groundwork read. An actual incident at a Western mission in Moscow inside the same window confirms the pre-accusation read instead, and this desk should be scored against.

brief.head: Trump's $5,000 check collides with a 5.36pc thirty-year yield
brief.h: The president promised every American adult $5,000 and announced $500 rebates for roughly a million Obamacare customers eight weeks before the midterms, on the same day the Supreme Court blocked his party's Missouri congressional map and the long end of the Treasury curve hit its red line.
brief.t: Two branches of the same government are pulling the same rope in opposite directions, and the bond market is the rope. The fiscal side is loosening into an election - $5,000 a head is more than $1tn, on top of a debt stack already north of $37tn - while the monetary side is being pushed to tighten into an oil shock six days from now. Putnam called this the two-level game: a leader plays a foreign board and a domestic board simultaneously, and the moves that win one can lose the other. Here the domestic board is a five-seat House majority and the foreign board is the auction desk, where roughly $9tn of debt has to be rolled in the next year. The thirty-year at 5.36 per cent is not an opinion about Trump; it is the price a lender charges for thirty years of that combination. Note the tell: the same week produced two DIFFERENT instruments aimed at the same majority - a cash promise and a redrawn map - and the court took the map away.
brief.context: The caveat that carries this story is announcement versus instrument. There is no bill, no sponsor, no CBO score and no appropriation for the $5,000; two promises of exactly this shape have already been made this cycle - the DOGE savings dividend and the $2,000 tariff cheque - and neither was paid. The $500 ACA rebate is different in kind because it uses existing administrative authority and a defined population, which is why it can be announced with a date. Distinguishing those two is the whole read: one is a turnout instrument, the other is a payment. The CONSTRAINT on the fiscal side is not the president's preference but the maturity wall - the 2021-22 issuance vintage was sold at near-zero coupons and is being refinanced at five, which mechanically grows the interest line whatever anyone promises. On the electoral side, the Missouri ruling matters more than its one seat: mid-decade re-redistricting was the cheapest available way to move a five-seat margin, and the Supreme Court has now blocked it twice, which pushes the campaign back onto expensive instruments like transfers. BASE RATE for the reader to hold: pre-election cash transfers are common and their measured effect on vote share is small and short-lived, while their effect on the inflation expectations embedded in the long end is durable - which is the asymmetry that makes this a plumbing story rather than a politics story. Falsifier: introduced bill text with a sponsor and a score before November converts this from instrument to policy, and this read should be revised.

consp.claim: The dominant board reading is not that the money will arrive but that the promise itself is a distress signal: threads ask why an administration describing an 'economic golden age' with 'an assured victory' would need to promise $1.5tn, and answer that someone knows a break is coming. A parallel line runs the arithmetic straight - 'JUST ADD $1.3 TRILLION TO THE $40 TRILLION DEBT, BRO' - and treats the Supreme Court's Missouri ruling as evidence the majority is already gone.
consp.spread: A /biz/ thread explicitly asking how it hits the 10-year and 30-year, plus multiple /pol/ threads; the framing crosses the political divide, which is unusual and worth noting on its own.
consp.read: This maps onto the 'they know something' frame, and its checkable kernel is the strongest of any board narrative today - the fiscal-monetary collision is real, dateable and priced in the thirty-year yield. Where it overreaches is in inferring private knowledge from a public incentive: an administration eight weeks from a midterm with a five-seat margin has an entirely sufficient reason to promise money, and no inside information is required to explain it. The honest version of the boards' question is the one this desk asks in the card - is there a bill? Absent bill text, this is a turnout instrument and should be scored as one.

watch: The war-risk quotation at Bab el-Mandeb. It currently sits near 0.5 per cent of hull value and the industry's stated working assumption is that the Houthi threat is confined to Saudi-linked tonnage. The observable that converts a land advance into a world event is a quote that stops making that distinction - not a missile, a sentence.

Weekly Bab el-Mandeb transit counts for the weeks to 13 and 20 September against Lloyd's List Intelligence's published pre-Mocha baseline of 273 a week. Thursday's daily print was 12 against 30 the day before, with one vessel entering the Red Sea against seventeen. A weekly count holding near 270 means Mocha bought position; below roughly 150 means it bought closure.

Core CPI, then the FOMC on Wednesday, then the BoJ on Friday. Core PPI printed 0.2 against 0.3 expected - the one number still saying this is an energy shock rather than a general inflation. A hike into a soft core is a statement about the chair's credibility, not about barrels, and it is also the first leg of the August-2024 carry-unwind template that GEO-025 prices.

Whether Algiers names an Emirati asset. DP World holds thirty-year concessions over the container terminals at Algiers and Djen-Djen through fifty-fifty joint ventures with the Algerian port authorities. A published cancellation, suspension or non-renewal converts the rupture from gesture to instrument and resolves the new GEO-030; six months of silence with the terminals running normally kills it.

Bill text for the $5,000 dividend - a sponsor, a number, a CBO score - and separately, whether Moscow converts the FSB embassy case into expulsions of British diplomats within 30 days. Both are the same test in different theatres: does the announcement acquire an instrument, or was the announcement the whole product?
lesson: Today's lesson is about how a strait actually closes, and it is the difference between watching missiles and watching paperwork. Alfred Thayer Mahan's insight, written in 1890, was that sea power is not about owning ocean but about owning the narrow places where trade must pass - and Bab el-Mandeb, twenty-nine kilometres across, is one of about six such places on earth. But here is the part Mahan could not have known: a modern chokepoint does not shut when a ship is hit. It shuts when the Lloyd's Joint War Committee in London adds it to a listed area and underwriters stop distinguishing between classes of tonnage, because no owner sails a hull he cannot insure and no bank finances a cargo that cannot be covered. Call it closure by quotation. That is why this desk's tripwire is a war-risk quote and not a missile count - a threat that prices at half a per cent of hull value is a toll, and a threat that prices at three per cent is a closure, and the difference is made by an underwriting committee nobody elected. The base rate that should keep you calm and worried at once: the Suez Canal, shut in June 1967 when a land power held one bank, did not reopen until June 1975, and clearing it took roughly a year AFTER the political decision to reopen. Bank-held waterways stay shut for years; missile campaigns are measured in weeks. What that predicts now is testable - watch the weekly Bab el-Mandeb transit counts against the 273-a-week baseline published before Mocha fell, and watch whether one sentence in a war-risk quotation changes. If it does, the strait is closed no matter how quiet the shooting gets.

quiz.q: The brief argues that the Houthi capture of Mocha is more serious than two years of missile attacks on the same waterway. What is the stated mechanism?
options: Mocha is a large oil export terminal, so its loss removes supply from the market
Holding the bank of a 29km strait means shore-launched weapons fired from cover, which cannot be intercepted and can only be reversed by infantry the defending coalition does not have
The Houthis captured advanced anti-ship missiles stored in the port
Mocha gives the Houthis a seat at Yemen's peace negotiations
quiz.why: The distinction is between a threat that can be shot down and a threat that has to be taken back on the ground. Missile campaigns are measured in weeks; the Suez Canal, closed in 1967 when a land power held one bank, took until 1975 to reopen. That asymmetry, not the size of any single attack, is what changed on Thursday.

quiz.q: According to today's lesson, who actually decides whether a strait is 'closed'?
options: The navy with the most ships in the area
The United Nations Security Council, via a formal designation
War-risk underwriters - when a quotation stops distinguishing between classes of tonnage, owners stop sailing and banks stop financing cargo
The country that owns the nearest coastline
quiz.why: Call it closure by quotation. No owner sails a hull he cannot insure and no bank finances an uncoverable cargo, so the operative decision sits with the Lloyd's Joint War Committee and the P&I clubs rather than with any navy. That is why this desk's tripwire is a premium, not a missile count.

plumbing.epoch: E6, the 2008-2022 quantitative-easing rail in its unwind chapter, meeting E4, the 1973 security-for-barrels bargain, at the auction desk - and today a third rail joined them. E4's original bargain was American security guarantees in exchange for dollar-denominated oil, and it assumed the guarantor could keep the sea lanes open. Two chokepoints are now contested at once, Hormuz by permit and Bab el-Mandeb by ground, which means the security half of that 53-year-old bargain is being repriced at the same moment the monetary half is being asked to absorb a supply shock. The old rail: a central bank as the price-insensitive marginal buyer of long duration. The new permit: it is a seller, and the private buyers replacing it are pricing thirty years of inflation during a war over two of the six places on earth where seaborne trade must pass single file.

sections.t: US diesel set an all-time record this week at $5.820 a gallon, and the crack spread — the refiner's fee for turning crude into something an engine can burn — printed an all-time $108 a barrel while Brent sat at an unremarkable $96. In the same week US missiles reportedly struck a tanker at Iran's Kharg Island anchorage, and Ukrainian drones held Russian refinery runs at 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since May 2002.

Crude — the thing everyone photographs and embargoes — is behaving; refined product is not. A $108 crack means the market will pay more to convert a barrel than the barrel is worth: a fact about cokers and hydrotreaters, not about oil. Name the mechanism — the conversion bottleneck. The binding constraint is never the abundant input but the narrow step in the middle, which cannot be built on the timescale of a war or an election.

sections.h: Deep history I — Rockefeller never wanted the oil
sections.t: John D. Rockefeller owned almost no wells. He owned the refineries of Cleveland, and what he did with them in 1871 is the founding text of chokepoint economics. Tom Scott of the Pennsylvania Railroad chartered the South Improvement Company, and Rockefeller's terms inside it were breathtaking: the Erie, New York Central and Pennsylvania would pay the SIC a rebate of $1.06 on every barrel it shipped — and a drawback of $1.06 on every barrel shipped by refiners outside the club. He was paid when his rivals did business. The charter was repealed that April before a single transaction cleared, and Ida Tarbell's exposé later finished the job — but the insight outlived the scandal: crude is worthless until someone converts and moves it, and whoever owns the narrow step prices the wide one.

sections.h: Deep history II — the war decided at the still
sections.t: The largest test of this proposition was the Allied air war, fought inside the alliance before it was fought over Germany. Arthur Harris of RAF Bomber Command believed in punishment: burn the cities, break the will. Carl Spaatz and Arthur Tedder pushed what Harris dismissed as panacea targets — oil. Germany had almost no crude. It had Bergius hydrogenation, synthetic fuel pressed from coal at Leuna, Pölitz and Brüx, plants too enormous to hide. The oil plan began in May 1944. Leuna alone absorbed 22 raids, 6,552 bomber sorties and 18,328 tons of bombs across a year, behind Europe's heaviest flak concentration. It worked anyway. German synthetic output fell from a peak of 316,000 tons a month to 107,000 in June 1944 and 17,000 by September. Aviation gasoline — the specific fraction, not oil in general — went from 175,000 tons in April to 5,000 in September: 97% gone in five months. From May 1944 Germany consumed more than it produced every month, and the stockpile was gone in six.

sections.h: Deep history II — the fuel, not the factories
sections.t: The detail that makes it unforgettable: over the same period Albert Speer drove German tank and aircraft PRODUCTION to its wartime peak. The Reich ended 1944 with more airframes than it could fly and more panzers than it could move — the factories were fine and the fuel was not. The US Strategic Bombing Survey — written by people with every reason to praise bombing in general — judged the oil and transport campaigns decisive and the city campaign not. Japan lost the same way: the July 1941 freeze is remembered as an oil embargo, but the fatal shortage was 100-octane aviation gasoline, a conversion capability Japan could not build.

sections.h: Deep history III — how the West stopped building stills
sections.t: Now the slow part. The last greenfield major refinery built in the United States was Marathon's Garyville, Louisiana: built 1973-76, online 1977, still running at 596,000 barrels a day. Fifty years, no new plants — and the base is now shrinking: about 132 operable refineries in January 2025 against more than 300 in 1981, with roughly 1.235m b/d of distillation capacity removed in seven recent closures and conversions, over 6.5% of the total. All of it while shale made America the largest crude producer in history at 13.86m b/d. The country built the well and stopped building the still. The capacity emigrated rather than vanished — Jamnagar runs 1.24m b/d, Dangote opened at 650,000 and plans 1.4m, China kept building — so the toll moved east and south, to jurisdictions happy to buy discounted sanctioned crude and sell the product back to the people imposing the sanctions.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: In all three cases the scarce thing is the transformation, and transformation capacity is inelastic over any politically relevant horizon: a new crude supplier takes a fortnight, a new hydrocracker takes five years and a billion dollars. Ukraine is now running the 1944 oil plan at a ten-thousandth of the cost, a drone flying 1,550km to Omsk doing what 6,552 B-17 sorties did to Leuna — Pape's denial thesis tested live. It breaks against me here: Germany had no crude and no neutral supplier, Russia has both, and a 24-year low in refining has not stopped Pokrovsk.

sections.h: The adjudication — Yergin and Blas vs Chris Miller
sections.t: THE ADJUDICATION — YERGIN AND BLAS versus CHRIS MILLER Yergin and Blas hold that energy chokepoints self-heal — inventories, bypass and rerouting absorb shocks forecast to be fatal — and they have been right about the barrel, Brent at $96 in a war that curtailed over 11m b/d. Chris Miller's Chip War argues the opposite for inputs that are not fungible: no reserve of fabs, no bypass for EUV, a decade to rebuild. The evidence splits them by step. Yergin and Blas won the crude argument; the crack is the market announcing the win does not survive one step downstream, because there is no strategic reserve of cokers — the US holds hundreds of millions of barrels of crude in the SPR and about a million barrels of distillate in the Northeast reserve, having stockpiled the input it cannot burn. Miller's case is still weaker in oil than in silicon: diesel is shippable in a way a fab's output is not, so refining heals in 12-24 months rather than 12-24 days.

OECD gasoline demand is in structural decline as EVs scale; diesel and jet demand are not, because trucks, ships, aircraft, mining and data-centre backup have no substitute. But a refinery makes every cut at once, so the economics that close Western refineries — falling gasoline — destroy the distillate capacity nobody meant to lose. A trap, not a cycle; confidence high. The bolder call, near 60%: by the mid-2030s the US is at once the world's largest crude exporter and a chronic net importer of middle distillates, and that buys a strategic PRODUCT reserve — legislated storage of diesel and jet, enacted after a winter shortage rather than before one. What keeps this honest is GEO-026: does the US diesel crack settle below $45 before 15 December 2026? It sits at 35%, so the house is 65% on regime rather than outage — and if the crack mean-reverts on the 2022 schedule, this is an elegant story about a spike, published as a miss.
